newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperforming the bloc.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperforming the bloc.

text.p: Australian bond yields underperformed against the bloc after data showed a pick-up in wages growth through enterprise bargaining agreements.

Long-dated yields had dipped to their lowest level since February in after-hours trading following a rally in U.S. Treasuries on the unchanged policy stance by the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.

However, the local move was seen overdone, and with local private wage agreements coming out at 4.8 percent in annualised average terms in the March quarter, the market was quick to reverse the move, traders said.
This saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widened out to around 100 basis points.
"In the near term, we expect the 10-year Aussie-U.S. spread to trade in the 90-120 basis point range," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank Australia.

"As continued signs of a strengthening economy, and possible wage and inflationary concerns further down the track emerge, the spread could widen towards the 150 bp mark at the end of the year," she added.
The largest move on the day was against Canada, which outperformed the U.S. following the Fed news as it relieved pressure on the Canadian dollar.
